config.title: Build a shopping cart quantity manager

intro.title: Build a shopping cart quantity manager
intro.body: In this lesson, you will build a shopping cart quantity manager that allows users to increase, decrease, and reset the quantity of an item. You'll learn how to use JavaScript state to track and update the quantity value dynamically. The main technologies involved are JavaScript variables, event handlers, and DOM manipulation to reflect changes on the page. By the end, you'll have a functional interface that responds to user clicks and maintains the correct count.
intro.usecase: This quantity manager pattern appears in virtually every e-commerce platform where users adjust item quantities in their shopping cart. You'll see this exact UI component on sites like Amazon, Target, or Shopify stores when customers increase or decrease quantities before checkout. As a developer, you'll implement similar controls for subscription services where users modify plan quantities, or in restaurant apps where customers adjust meal portions. Mastering this pattern is essential for building any interactive shopping experience where users need to modify item counts in real-time.

objectives: Initialize state variables to track product quantities in a shopping cart
Implement functions to increment and decrement item quantities
Render dynamic quantity displays that update based on state changes
Bind event handlers to buttons for user interaction with quantity controls
Apply conditional logic to prevent quantities from dropping below zero
Construct a complete quantity manager interface with all interactive elements
Manipulate the DOM to reflect real-time quantity updates

steps.title: Import React and useState
steps.instruction: Import React and the useState hook from the 'react' package.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in React and useState from 'react'.
steps.analogousExample:
// Importing React and a hook
import React, { useState } from 'react';
steps.expectedOutcome: You'll have React and useState available to use in your shopping cart quantity manager.
successCriteria: React and useState are imported from 'react'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure you're importing both React and useState from 'react'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to import both React and useState from the 'react' package.

steps.title: Create the ShoppingCart component
steps.instruction: Create a functional component named ShoppingCart that returns an empty React fragment (<></>) for now.
steps.hint: Define a function called ShoppingCart that returns JSX. You can use either a function declaration or arrow function syntax.
steps.seedCode:
import React, { useState } from 'react';

// Create the ShoppingCart component here
steps.expectedOutcome: You should have a ShoppingCart component that returns an empty fragment.
successCriteria: A component named ShoppingCart is defined and returns an empty fragment.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you've defined a component named ShoppingCart that returns an empty fragment (<></>).
steps.feedbackWrong: The component isn't defined correctly. Create a function named ShoppingCart that returns an empty fragment.

steps.title: Initialize cart quantity state
steps.instruction: Inside the ShoppingCart component, use useState to create a state variable named quantity and initialize it to 0.
steps.hint: Call useState with the initial value 0 and destructure the returned array into two variables: quantity and setQuantity.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: creating a state variable
const [count, setCount] = useState(0);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a quantity state variable that starts at 0, ready to track cart items.
successCriteria: The component contains a useState call that creates a quantity variable initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure you're using useState with 0 as the initial value and naming the variable 'quantity'.
steps.feedbackWrong: That doesn't look right. Remember to call useState(0) and destructure [quantity, setQuantity] inside the component.

steps.title: Create increment handler function
steps.instruction: Inside your ShoppingCart component, create a function named handleIncrement that increases the quantity state by 1.
steps.hint: Define a function that uses the setQuantity function to update the state value.
steps.expectedOutcome: A handleIncrement function is defined inside the component that increments the quantity state.
successCriteria: The handleIncrement function is defined and uses setQuantity to increase quantity by 1.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've created a function, but make sure it properly increments the quantity state using setQuantity.
steps.feedbackWrong: The increment handler function is not yet defined or doesn't increment the quantity state correctly.

steps.title: Add main container and title
steps.instruction: In your ShoppingCart component's return statement, replace the current return value with a div element that has a className of 'cart-container', containing an h1 element with the text 'Shopping Cart'.
steps.hint:
Remember to use JSX syntax: return (

Shopping Cart

);
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now returns a structured container with a title, providing the foundation for the shopping cart UI.
successCriteria: The return statement contains a div with className 'cart-container' and an h1 element with the text 'Shopping Cart'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure your return statement includes both the div with className 'cart-container' and the h1 with 'Shopping Cart' text.
steps.feedbackWrong: The return statement doesn't match the expected structure. Check that you're returning a div with className 'cart-container' containing an h1 element.

steps.title: Display current quantity
steps.instruction: Inside the ShoppingCart component's return statement, add a paragraph element that displays the current quantity value with the text 'Quantity: [value]'.
steps.hint:
Use JSX to create a

element and embed the quantity state variable inside curly braces to display its current value.
steps.analogousExample:
// Displaying a state value in JSX

Current count: {count}
steps.expectedOutcome: The UI will show the current quantity value (starting at 0) in a paragraph element.
successCriteria: A paragraph element with the text 'Quantity: ' followed by the quantity state value is added to the return statement.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a paragraph, but make sure it displays the quantity state variable with the exact text format 'Quantity: [value]'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The paragraph element displaying the quantity value is missing or incorrect. Check that you're using the quantity variable inside curly braces.

steps.title: Add increment button and wire click handler
steps.instruction: Add a button element with the text '+ Add Item' inside the main container. Set its onClick event handler to call the handleIncrement function.
steps.hint: Use the <button> tag with the onClick attribute. Remember to reference the handler function without calling it (no parentheses).
steps.analogousExample:
// Adding a button with a click handler
<button onClick={handleClick}>Click me</button>
steps.expectedOutcome: A button labeled '+ Add Item' appears in the UI that, when clicked, increases the quantity by 1.
successCriteria: A <button> element exists with text '+ Add Item'
The button's onClick attribute is set to {handleIncrement}
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a button, but make sure it has the correct text '+ Add Item' and the onClick handler is properly set to handleIncrement.
steps.feedbackWrong: The button isn't correctly implemented. Check that you've added a <button> element with the specified text and onClick handler.

steps.title: Add decrement and reset buttons with handlers
steps.instruction: Add two new button elements inside the main container: one with text '- Remove Item' that calls handleDecrement when clicked, and another with text 'Reset Cart' that calls handleReset when clicked.
steps.hint: Place the buttons after the existing increment button. Use the onClick attribute to wire each button to its corresponding handler function.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have three interactive buttons: one to increase quantity, one to decrease it, and one to reset to zero.
successCriteria: Two new button elements are added with correct text labels and wired to their respective handler functions via onClick.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Nice! Proceed to the next step.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added buttons, but check that each has the correct text and onClick handler. The decrement button should call handleDecrement, and the reset button should call handleReset.
steps.feedbackWrong: The buttons are missing or not correctly wired. Add two button elements with '- Remove Item' and 'Reset Cart' text, each with an onClick attribute pointing to the appropriate handler.
